The incident tables, narratives and summaries agree on this count and on the ordinal numbering (second in Q2, third in Q3). [S9] [S7] [S3] [S1] [S2] [S4] [S5] [S8] [S6]

# 2024 Incident Reports: Incident Count by Service

## Executive summary
Database had the most incidents in the 2024 incident reports, with 3 of the 9 incidents recorded. Payments had 2. Auth, Search, API gateway and Checkout had 1 each. The count covers Q1–Q3 only, because no Q4 report was provided. All three Database incidents were attributed to disk-full failures. One Payments incident was blamed on database connection pool exhaustion. Depending on how that incident is attributed, the Database lead could be larger.

## Findings
### Database is the most frequent service (3 incidents)
Database had three incidents: INC-101 on 2024-01-14 (240 min), INC-202 on 2024-05-21 (180 min) and INC-302 on 2024-08-19 (120 min). All three had a disk-full root cause. The Q3 narrative calls the August outage the same class of failure as the two earlier database outages. [S1] [S2] [S3] [S4] [S5] [S6] [S7] [S10]

### Payments is second (2 incidents)
Payments had INC-102 on 2024-02-02 (95 min, connection pool exhaustion) and INC-303 on 2024-09-30 (150 min, third-party payment gateway outage). The Q3 narrative says the September outage was at the vendor and outside the organisation's control. [S3] [S6] [S7] [S10]

### Other services had 1 incident each
Auth had INC-103 on 2024-03-03 (30 min, expired TLS certificate). Search had INC-301 on 2024-07-08 (25 min, index corruption, fixed by rebuilding the index). API gateway had INC-201 on 2024-04-09 (60 min, misconfigured rate limit). Checkout had INC-203 on 2024-06-12 (45 min, connection pool exhaustion). [S3] [S4] [S6] [S7] [S10]

### Totals reconcile with the quarterly summaries
The Q1–Q3 reports contain 9 incidents, 3 per quarter, across 6 distinct services. The quarterly summaries match the incident tables. [S1] [S2] [S3] [S4] [S5] [S6]

### Attribution caveat: connection pool exhaustion
The Feb 2 incident is listed under Payments, but the Q1 narrative says the cause was exhaustion of the database connection pool. Counting by root-cause component could treat it as Database-related. Counting by affected service, as the tables do, gives Database 3 and Payments 2. [S3] [S7]

### Minor wording difference on the Aug 19 root cause
The Q3 table and summary say "Disk full", while the narrative says a log volume filling up. The narrative treats it as the same class of failure, so this is probably a wording difference and not a real conflict. [S5] [S6] [S10]

### Support tickets were not counted as incidents
The support tickets use categories that overlap with service names (database, payments, search, auth, checkout, api, billing). They are not incident reports, so they were excluded from the counts. Some tickets share dates with incidents: database tickets on 2024-05-21 and 2024-08-19, and a search ticket on 2024-07-09. The ticket category "api" compares with the incident service "API gateway", and "billing" has no matching incident service. [S4] [S9]

## Recommendations
- Report Database as the service with the most incidents (3 of 9) in Q1–Q3 2024, and state clearly that the count excludes Q4.
- State the counting basis (affected service as listed in the incident tables), and note that the Feb 2 Payments incident involved the database connection pool.
- Given that all three Database incidents were disk-full failures, look at disk capacity as the recurring cause. The Q1 narrative notes that no disk usage alert existed at the time of the January outage.
- Obtain the Q4 2024 report before giving a full-year ranking.

## Missing information
- No Q4 2024 incident report was provided, so the counts are for Q1–Q3 only.
- The Q2 narrative is not provided. Only the Q2 summary and table are available.
- Some tickets have no matching incident in the reports: T-1017 (billing, 2024-07-30), T-1018 (api, 2024-08-01), T-1020 (auth, 2024-08-28), T-1022 (checkout, 2024-10-05) and T-1023 (search, 2024-10-12). The sources do not say whether these were incidents.
- Ticket T-1015 (payments, 2024-06-13) falls one day after the Checkout incident INC-203 (2024-06-12), and no Payments incident was reported in June. The sources do not explain the link, if any.
- The security policy is about disclosure timelines and gives no service names or incident counts.
per_question.judge: gemini-2.5-flash: The system answer correctly identifies the database as the service with the most incidents and provides the correct number of incidents and the incident IDs.

# Summary of Recommended Fixes Across Quarterly Incident Reports

## Executive summary
Only one document, the Q2 2024 postmortem, lists recommended fixes (S6). It has three actions: automate database volume expansion, review rate limit changes before deployment, and run quarterly failover drills. The Q1 and Q3 reports have no postmortem actions. Disk-full database outages recurred in all three quarters (240, 180 and 120 minutes). The sources don't show whether the Q2 volume-expansion action was implemented. Connection pool exhaustion, TLS certificate renewal and third-party gateway dependency have no documented remediation. No action has an owner, deadline or status.

## Findings
### Recurring disk-full database outage is the dominant theme
Disk-full database outages occurred in Q1 (INC-101, 240 min), Q2 (INC-202, 180 min) and Q3 (INC-302, 120 min). The only explicit remediation is the Q2 postmortem action to automate database volume expansion. The Q1 narrative says no disk usage alert existed at the time, which implies an alert could be added. No source states that as an action. [S2] [S3] [S1] [S9] [S5] [S7] [S6] [S8]

### Q2 postmortem lists three actions
The Q2 postmortem actions are: automate database volume expansion, review rate limit changes before deployment, and run quarterly failover drills. The rate limit review addresses INC-201, the misconfigured rate limit incident on the API gateway. [S6] [S3]

### Possible gap between the Q2 action and the Q3 root cause
The Q3 incident table gives the August 19 root cause as 'Disk full'. The Q3 narrative attributes it to a log volume filling up. This is probably the same failure class. However, the Q2 action to automate database volume expansion may not cover a log volume. The Q3 outage also happened after that action was proposed. [S1] [S8] [S5] [S6]

### Connection pool exhaustion has no documented fix
Connection pool exhaustion caused INC-102 (Payments, 95 min, Q1) and INC-203 (Checkout, 45 min, Q2). The Q1 narrative says it happened under peak load. No source recommends a fix. [S2] [S3] [S9]

### Expired TLS certificate has no documented remediation
The Q1 Auth incident (INC-103) was caused by an expired TLS certificate that nobody was assigned to renew. This suggests an ownership or renewal-process fix, but none is documented. [S2] [S9]

### Q3 search and payments incidents
The Q3 search index corruption (INC-301) was fixed by rebuilding the index. That is a corrective action, not a preventive one. The Q3 payments incident (INC-303) was a third-party gateway outage that the narrative describes as outside the organisation's control. No mitigation is proposed. [S8] [S1]

## Recommendations
- Confirm whether the Q2 action to automate database volume expansion was implemented. Also confirm whether it covers log volumes, given the Q3 outage was attributed to a log volume filling up (S6, S8, S1).
- Consider formally adding disk usage alerting as an action, because the Q1 narrative notes none existed. No source currently records this as an action (S9).
- Document remediation for connection pool exhaustion, which caused two incidents in two quarters (S2, S3, S9).
- Consider assigning ownership for TLS certificate renewal, since the Q1 expiry happened because nobody was assigned (S9).
- Decide whether any mitigation is needed for the third-party payment gateway dependency. The Q3 report only describes the outage as outside the organisation's control (S8).
- Record an owner, deadline and status for each postmortem action, and produce action lists for Q1 and Q3 (S6).

## Missing information
- Postmortem actions for Q1 and Q3. The only action list is from Q2 (S6).
- Evidence that the Q2 volume-expansion action was implemented.
- Owners, deadlines and completion status for any action.
- Documented remediation for connection pool exhaustion, TLS certificate renewal and third-party gateway dependency.
- A documented disk usage alerting action.
- The security policy (S10) covers disclosure timelines only and doesn't relate to the operational fixes. None of the incidents is described as affecting customer data.
per_question.judge: gemini-2.5-flash: The answer lists some of the recommended fixes but misses several, such as disk usage alerts, certificate renewal ownership, larger connection pools, and a fallback payment provider.
